# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to

Since hosts and the CLI share ONE log file (`~/.fah/logs/fa.log`), interleaved host lines can't be attributed to a session/run while CLI lines can. The claimed "post-mortem-identical / same greps work" is materially overstated: `grep 'tool start sid='` won't match host lines, and correlating a host's interleaved lines with a specific run is impossible (no session id, no run id). The sink has no way to know the session id, and AgentCoreServices has none either. `browser` + `browser_eval` in `agent_cli_tools.dart`

- `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — `fa serve --bridge [--port N] [--token T]`
  loopback WebSocket bridge (binds 127.0.0.1 only, AC15; non-
  `chrome-extension://` origins refused): one-time token pairing
  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),
  two-way mail relay over the messaging fabric, ping/pong keepalive,
  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs

Now, a subtle parity issue for `resolveEndpointKey`: the OLD version, for a default endpoint, returned `_genuineEnvValue(...)` — the env VALUE. `browser` + `browser_eval` in `agent_cli_tools.dart`

- `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — `fa serve --bridge [--port N] [--token T]`
  loopback WebSocket bridge (binds 127.0.0.1 only, AC15; non-
  `chrome-extension://` origins refused): one-time token pairing
  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),
  two-way mail relay over the messaging fabric, ping/pong keepalive,
  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.

  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),

  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.

The new `FileAgentTelemetrySink` writes lines WITHOUT the `sid=` field: `run start`, `turn start`, `tool start name=bash`, `turn end stop=stop elapsed=7s`. The PR claims "the SAME `<iso8601> <message>` lines as the CLI" and "post-mortem-identical; grep one log for either" and "the CLI's own fa.log fidelity... line-for-line (issue #1322 AC: the same fidelity for an in-process host)". But the lines lack `sid=`, which the CLI deliberately adds ("parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"). Since hosts and the CLI share ONE log file (`~/.fah/logs/fa.log`), interleaved host lines can't be attributed to a session/run while CLI lines can. The claimed "post-mortem-identical / same greps work" is materially overstated: `grep 'tool start sid='` won't match host lines, and correlating a host's interleaved lines with a specific run is impossible (no session id, no run id). The sink has no way to know the session id, and AgentCoreServices has none either. ## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

tests are done right:

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).

  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).

  `lib/src/cli/browser_bridge_commands.dart` (`/browser connect|status`).
- `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — `fa serve --bridge [--port N] [--token T]`
  loopback WebSocket bridge (binds 127.0.0.1 only, AC15; non-
  `chrome-extension://` origins refused): one-time token pairing
  (`.fah/bridge/token`, 0600, minted fresh per `/browser connect`),
  two-way mail relay over the messaging fabric, ping/pong keepalive,
  `browserReq`/`browserRes` correlation for the `browser_*` tools. The
  CLI mounts the same server in-process via `bin/fah.dart`'s
  `_FaBrowserBridgeHandle` (also the `BrowserController` seam).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).

Important: when the stream function THROWS, the loop's `_providerErrorTurn` converts the error to a terminal message with `'$error'` — i.e. `error.toString()`. The telemetry wrap instead converts the throw to an ErrorEvent whose `errorMessage` is `formatProviderError(error)`.

Difference:
- Without telemetry: throw → loop `_providerErrorTurn` → `errorMessage: '$error'` (e.g. `ProviderHttpError: 502, bad gateway` or whatever toString is).

The PR claims "the SAME `<iso8601> <message>` lines as the CLI" and "post-mortem-identical; grep one log for either" and "the CLI's own fa.log fidelity... line-for-line (issue #1322 AC: the same fidelity for an in-process host)". Now, a subtle parity issue for `resolveEndpointKey`: the OLD version, for a default endpoint, returned `_genuineEnvValue(...)` — the env VALUE. The new version returns `env` only if `envNames.contains(name)`. Consider: default endpoint, legacy store entry for `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (leg 3), and a genuine env value for a DIFFERENT env name that equals its store entry (not genuine). Important: when the stream function THROWS, the loop's `_providerErrorTurn` converts the error to a terminal message with `'$error'` — i.e. `error.toString()`. The telemetry wrap instead converts the throw to an ErrorEvent whose `errorMessage` is `formatProviderError(error)`.

Difference:
- Without telemetry: throw → loop `_providerErrorTurn` → `errorMessage: '$error'` (e.g. `ProviderHttpError: 502, bad gateway` or whatever toString is).
- With telemetry: throw → wrap catches → ErrorEvent with `errorMessage: formatProviderError(error)` (e.g. `502: bad gateway`) → loop treats it as a normal in-stream error event.

So the observable transcript/errorMessage text DIFFERS between wrapped and unwrapped stream functions for the same provider throw. `formatProviderError` is likely nicer, but it IS a behavioral change in the error surface when telemetry is enabled — errors that used to render as `$error` now render as the provider-formatted message. Also `assistantMessage` fields differ: `_terminalMessage(config.model, ...)` presumably builds message with api/provider/model from config.model, usage zero — the wrap's `_errorEventFor` builds an AssistantMessage too with similar fields. Both converge to an error turn. The loop then processes the ErrorEvent through `_finishStreamed` — same path as in-stream provider errors (retry logic! maxEmptyRetries? Now I see the CLI's actual fa.log line format:

- `'run start sid=$_logSid'` — includes **sid=** (short session id)!
- `'turn start sid=$_logSid'`
- `'tool start sid=$_logSid name=$toolName'`
- `'tool end sid=$_logSid name=$toolName error=$isError'`
- `'turn end sid=$_logSid stop=${message.stopReason.name}'`

The new `FileAgentTelemetrySink` writes lines WITHOUT the `sid=` field: `run start`, `turn start`, `tool start name=bash`, `turn end stop=stop elapsed=7s`. The PR claims "the SAME `<iso8601> <message>` lines as the CLI" and "post-mortem-identical; grep one log for either" and "the CLI's own fa.log fidelity... line-for-line (issue #1322 AC: the same fidelity for an in-process host)". But the lines lack `sid=`, which the CLI deliberately adds ("parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"). Since hosts and the CLI share ONE log file (`~/.fah/logs/fa.log`), interleaved host lines can't be attributed to a session/run while CLI lines can. The claimed "post-mortem-identical / same greps work" is materially overstated: `grep 'tool start sid='` won't match host lines, and correlating a host's interleaved lines with a specific run is impossible (no session id, no run id). The sink has no way to know the session id, and AgentCoreServices has none either. This is a real gap vs the stated AC — I'd rate this IMPORTANT (maintainability/forensics fidelity gap, misleading doc claims) — arguably it's the core deliverable promise of Gap 3. Not blocking (functionality works), but the "identical" claim is wrong. Also `elapsed=` on turn end is an ADDITION not in the CLI's format; plus `run error ... http=`. Those extensions are documented. The missing sid is the fidelity gap.

Important: when the stream function THROWS, the loop's `_providerErrorTurn` converts the error to a terminal message with `'$error'` — i.e. `error.toString()`. The telemetry wrap instead converts the throw to an ErrorEvent whose `errorMessage` is `formatProviderError(error)`.

Difference:
- Without telemetry: throw → loop `_providerErrorTurn` → `errorMessage: '$error'` (e.g. `ProviderHttpError: 502, bad gateway` or whatever toString is).
- With telemetry: throw → wrap catches → ErrorEvent with `errorMessage: formatProviderError(error)` (e.g. `502: bad gateway`) → loop treats it as a normal in-stream error event.

So the observable transcript/errorMessage text DIFFERS between wrapped and unwrapped stream functions for the same provider throw. `formatProviderError` is likely nicer, but it IS a behavioral change in the error surface when telemetry is enabled — errors that used to render as `$error` now render as the provider-formatted message. Also `assistantMessage` fields differ: `_terminalMessage(config.model, ...)` presumably builds message with api/provider/model from config.model, usage zero — the wrap's `_errorEventFor` builds an AssistantMessage too with similar fields. Important: when the stream function THROWS, the loop's `_providerErrorTurn` converts the error to a terminal message with `'$error'` — i.e. `error.toString()`. The telemetry wrap instead converts the throw to an ErrorEvent whose `errorMessage` is `formatProviderError(error)`.

Difference:
- Without telemetry: throw → loop `_providerErrorTurn` → `errorMessage: '$error'` (e.g. `ProviderHttpError: 502, bad gateway` or whatever toString is).
- With telemetry: throw → wrap catches → ErrorEvent with `errorMessage: formatProviderError(error)` (e.g. `502: bad gateway`) → loop treats it as a normal in-stream error event.

So the observable transcript/errorMessage text DIFFERS between wrapped and unwrapped stream functions for the same provider throw. `formatProviderError` is likely nicer, but it IS a behavioral change in the error surface when telemetry is enabled — errors that used to render as `$error` now render as the provider-formatted message. Also `assistantMessage` fields differ: `_terminalMessage(config.model, ...)` presumably builds message with api/provider/model from config.model, usage zero — the wrap's `_errorEventFor` builds an AssistantMessage too with similar fields. Both converge to an error turn. The loop then processes the ErrorEvent through `_finishStreamed` — same path as in-stream provider errors (retry logic! maxEmptyRetries? Let me check whether ErrorEvent triggers retries differently than a thrown error).

Actually the more subtle difference: retry/fallback behavior. A thrown streamFunction error goes through `_providerErrorTurn` directly — no retries. An ErrorEvent terminal goes through `_finishStreamed` — and possibly the empty-retry logic (`maxEmptyRetries` applies to degenerate-empty responses where stopReason == error with empty content? line 1604 area). OK — degenerate-empty only applies to `stop` reason, not error. So the wrap's ErrorEvent conversion doesn't introduce retry differences (an error stop always ends the run via `_terminalRunMessages`).

The remaining behavioral difference: the errorMessage text for a thrown error differs (`formatProviderError(error)` vs `'$error'`). Also the wrap changes WHEN the error surfaces: the loop calls streamFunction synchronously; legacy throw propagates through `_providerErrorTurn` immediately. With the wrap, the throw is caught inside the wrap and delivered as an ErrorEvent through the stream — the loop handles it in `_streamAssistantResponse`'s `await for`. Both end the run with StopReason.error. So behavior parity is preserved modulo the error message text. That's actually arguably an improvement (consistent provider-formatted errors), but it IS a subtle difference between telemetry-on and telemetry-off paths. The PR description presents this as intentional ("The providers-never-throw conversion for an exception that escaped a provider stream"). I'll note it as a SUGGESTION-level observation (behavioral asymmetry documented in code but worth noting: telemetry ON changes error text vs OFF — could surprise a host toggling telemetry and comparing transcripts). Actually more important: the message the agent sees / that goes into the transcript differs. Since telemetry is a debug facility, changing error semantics when enabled is a bit surprising, but the conversion happens to match what real provider adapters do (they never throw). Now I see the CLI's actual fa.log line format:

- `'run start sid=$_logSid'` — includes **sid=** (short session id)!
- `'turn start sid=$_logSid'`
- `'tool start sid=$_logSid name=$toolName'`
- `'tool end sid=$_logSid name=$toolName error=$isError'`
- `'turn end sid=$_logSid stop=${message.stopReason.name}'`

The new `FileAgentTelemetrySink` writes lines WITHOUT the `sid=` field: `run start`, `turn start`, `tool start name=bash`, `turn end stop=stop elapsed=7s`. The PR claims "the SAME `<iso8601> <message>` lines as the CLI" and "post-mortem-identical; grep one log for either" and "the CLI's own fa.log fidelity... line-for-line (issue #1322 AC: the same fidelity for an in-process host)". But the lines lack `sid=`, which the CLI deliberately adds ("parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"). Since hosts and the CLI share ONE log file (`~/.fah/logs/fa.log`), interleaved host lines can't be attributed to a session/run while CLI lines can. The claimed "post-mortem-identical / same greps work" is materially overstated: `grep 'tool start sid='` won't match host lines, and correlating a host's interleaved lines with a specific run is impossible (no session id, no run id). The sink has no way to know the session id, and AgentCoreServices has none either. This is a real gap vs the stated AC — I'd rate this IMPORTANT (maintainability/forensics fidelity gap, misleading doc claims) — arguably it's the core deliverable promise of Gap 3. Not blocking (functionality works), but the "identical" claim is wrong. Also `elapsed=` on turn end is an ADDITION not in the CLI's format; plus `run error ... http=`. Those extensions are documented. The missing sid is the fidelity gap.

Also worth checking where `run end` / `run error` lines exist in the CLI... `approval_commands.dart` shows run start / turn start / tool start / tool end / turn end. Let me check for 'run end' / heartbeat / stuck lines and http status lines to compare vocabularies.

Important: when the stream function THROWS, the loop's `_providerErrorTurn` converts the error to a terminal message with `'$error'` — i.e. `error.toString()`. The telemetry wrap instead converts the throw to an ErrorEvent whose `errorMessage` is `formatProviderError(error)`.

Difference:
- Without telemetry: throw → loop `_providerErrorTurn` → `errorMessage: '$error'` (e.g. `ProviderHttpError: 502, bad gateway` or whatever toString is).
- With telemetry: throw → wrap catches → ErrorEvent with `errorMessage: formatProviderError(error)` (e.g. `502: bad gateway`) → loop treats it as a normal in-stream error event.

So the observable transcript/errorMessage text DIFFERS between wrapped and unwrapped stream functions for the same provider throw. `formatProviderError` is likely nicer, but it IS a behavioral change in the error surface when telemetry is enabled — errors that used to render as `$error` now render as the provider-formatted message. Also `assistantMessage` fields differ: `_terminalMessage(config.model, ...)` presumably builds message with api/provider/model from config.model, usage zero — the wrap's `_errorEventFor` builds an AssistantMessage too with similar fields. **Gap 1 + Gap 4 — `docs/embedding.md`**: the canonical `wireAgentCore(...).buildAgentStack(...)` embed path for a desktop host — services bundle, canonical tools, watchdog defaults (run-idle 8 min, connect 180 s, stream-idle 300 s), stuck-tool heartbeats, cancel (`agent.abort()` / `agent.cancelToken` — the exact thing adk_dart's `Runner` lacks), key resolution, telemetry, and a keep-vs-delegate table. **Gap 2 — key resolution exposed to hosts (pure core, stores injected)**:

**Gap 3 — lifecycle telemetry (interface in core, file sink behind `lib/io.dart`)**:
- Pure core: `AgentTelemetrySink` + `AgentTelemetryEvent` + `InMemoryTelemetrySink` (bounded ring) + the adapter. Boundary note 1 honored: zero `dart:io` in the core chain.
- IO: `FileAgentTelemetrySink.forHomeDir(home)` → appends the CLI's exact `<iso8601> <message>` lines to the SAME `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` — host embeds and CLI sessions are post-mortem-identical; never throws.

Important: when the stream function THROWS, the loop's `_providerErrorTurn` converts the error to a terminal message with `'$error'` — i.e. `error.toString()`. The telemetry wrap instead converts the throw to an ErrorEvent whose `errorMessage` is `formatProviderError(error)`.

Difference:
- Without telemetry: throw → loop `_providerErrorTurn` → `errorMessage: '$error'` (e.g. `ProviderHttpError: 502, bad gateway` or whatever toString is).
- With telemetry: throw → wrap catches → ErrorEvent with `errorMessage: formatProviderError(error)` (e.g. `502: bad gateway`) → loop treats it as a normal in-stream error event.

So the observable transcript/errorMessage text DIFFERS between wrapped and unwrapped stream functions for the same provider throw. `formatProviderError` is likely nicer, but it IS a behavioral change in the error surface when telemetry is enabled — errors that used to render as `$error` now render as the provider-formatted message. Difference:
- Without telemetry: throw → loop `_providerErrorTurn` → `errorMessage: '$error'` (e.g. `ProviderHttpError: 502, bad gateway` or whatever toString is).
- With telemetry: throw → wrap catches → ErrorEvent with `errorMessage: formatProviderError(error)` (e.g. `502: bad gateway`) → loop treats it as a normal in-stream error event.

So the observable transcript/errorMessage text DIFFERS between wrapped and unwrapped stream functions for the same provider throw. `formatProviderError` is likely nicer, but it IS a behavioral change in the error surface when telemetry is enabled — errors that used to render as `$error` now render as the provider-formatted message. OK — degenerate-empty only applies to `stop` reason, not error. So the wrap's ErrorEvent conversion doesn't introduce retry differences (an error stop always ends the run via `_terminalRunMessages`).

The remaining behavioral difference: the errorMessage text for a thrown error differs (`formatProviderError(error)` vs `'$error'`). Also the wrap changes WHEN the error surfaces: the loop calls streamFunction synchronously; legacy throw propagates through `_providerErrorTurn` immediately. With the wrap, the throw is caught inside the wrap and delivered as an ErrorEvent through the stream — the loop handles it in `_streamAssistantResponse`'s `await for`. Both end the run with StopReason.error. So behavior parity is preserved modulo the error message text. That's actually arguably an improvement (consistent provider-formatted errors), but it IS a subtle difference between telemetry-on and telemetry-off paths. The PR description presents this as intentional ("The providers-never-throw conversion for an exception that escaped a provider stream"). I'll note it as a SUGGESTION-level observation (behavioral asymmetry documented in code but worth noting: telemetry ON changes error text vs OFF — could surprise a host toggling telemetry and comparing transcripts). Actually more important: the message the agent sees / that goes into the transcript differs. Since telemetry is a debug facility, changing error semantics when enabled is a bit surprising, but the conversion happens to match what real provider adapters do (they never throw). A host-supplied streamFunction that throws is out-of-contract anyway; the loop is "defensive anyway". So SUGGESTION.

Now I see the CLI's actual fa.log line format:

- `'run start sid=$_logSid'` — includes **sid=** (short session id)!
- `'turn start sid=$_logSid'`
- `'tool start sid=$_logSid name=$toolName'`
- `'tool end sid=$_logSid name=$toolName error=$isError'`
- `'turn end sid=$_logSid stop=${message.stopReason.name}'`

The new `FileAgentTelemetrySink` writes lines WITHOUT the `sid=` field: `run start`, `turn start`, `tool start name=bash`, `turn end stop=stop elapsed=7s`. The PR claims "the SAME `<iso8601> <message>` lines as the CLI" and "post-mortem-identical; grep one log for either" and "the CLI's own fa.log fidelity... line-for-line (issue #1322 AC: the same fidelity for an in-process host)". But the lines lack `sid=`, which the CLI deliberately adds ("parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"). Since hosts and the CLI share ONE log file (`~/.fah/logs/fa.log`), interleaved host lines can't be attributed to a session/run while CLI lines can. The claimed "post-mortem-identical / same greps work" is materially overstated: `grep 'tool start sid='` won't match host lines, and correlating a host's interleaved lines with a specific run is impossible (no session id, no run id). The sink has no way to know the session id, and AgentCoreServices has none either. Important detail: `formatProviderError` for `answeredHtml`/`answeredJson`/auth-redirect/empty-body cases does NOT render `<status>: ` — e.g. `'Request failed with status ${error.statusCode}'` (empty body) doesn't match `^(\d{3}): `. And `formatRateLimitMessage` renders `'<status>: <human>'` ✓. The empty-body case yields no status parse — but the typed `ProviderHttpError` branch in `_statusFromError` catches that directly (statusCode field). So `_statusFromError` handles typed errors fully; the string-parse fallback only applies to string errorMessage paths (in-stream ErrorEvents where the original error object is lost). For in-stream ErrorEvents, the errorMessage came from the provider adapters' own `formatProviderError` — consistent.

One more check on `_statusFromError`: it's called with `event.errorMessage` (a String) for in-stream ErrorEvents, and with thrown `error` objects in catch paths. In `_pump`: `if (event is ErrorEvent) _statusFromError(event.errorMessage);` — String branch. OK.

Subtle: `_statusFromError` keeps the LAST status. Multiple failed requests in one run (retry across turns): error record at run end carries the last failed status. Doc matches ("status of the failed request").

Now the CRITICAL correctness question I flagged: **aborted runs emit `run error`**. Let me trace once more:
1. User calls `agent.abort()` mid-request.
2. The loop: stream ends with aborted event OR `_abortedTurn` produces terminal message StopReason.aborted, errorMessage 'Operation aborted'.
3. AgentEndEvent messages include that terminal AssistantMessage with errorMessage != null.
4. `agentErrorMessage` returns 'Operation aborted' → `_emit(error, httpStatus: _lastHttpStatus, detail: 'Operation aborted')` → fa.log gets `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted`.

So yes — every user abort, every watchdog-cancel, every abort-driven run end logs `run error`. The CLI logs only `run end sid=…` for the same flow (it has no error line at all). For a host sharing fa.log, a forensics grep for `run error` now surfaces routine cancels. This dilutes the exact signal the issue cares about (real hangs/failures). It's a diagnostics-semantics bug worth IMPORTANT.

Wait — but is it possibly intended ("The terminal error of a finished run, or null on a clean run")? An aborted run is not a clean run. But the fa.log LINE label is `run error`, which reads as failure. And `runEnd.httpStatus` becomes null for aborted runs even if the last request 429'd. Design-wise I'd flag it: distinguish StopReason.error from StopReason.aborted in `agentErrorMessage`. IMPORTANT.

Now, another look at `AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` — it's PUBLIC. Why public? It's an instance method with no state use. Public surface bloat on the adapter; could be static or private. Minor SUGGESTION (API surface).

Also `_emit` for `error`: `httpStatus: httpStatus ?? _kindStatus(kind)` — passing `_lastHttpStatus` explicitly, `_kindStatus` returns `_lastHttpStatus` for error kind — redundant but harmless.

`runEnd`: `httpStatus: error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null` — for clean runs `_lastHttpStatus` is always null (never set on success) — so the doc "2xx when any token streamed" is dead text; runEnd NEVER carries a status in practice (error runs pass null explicitly; clean runs have null). So the httpStatus-on-runEnd feature is effectively UNIMPLEMENTED. That upgrades the doc-mismatch: the public API documents runEnd carrying "the status of the LAST request (2xx when any token streamed, else null)" but no code path can ever produce a non-null runEnd status. Either the implementation is missing the 2xx capture or the doc is wrong. IMPORTANT.

One question: the drift check resolves WITHOUT envNames — so for the DEFAULT catalog endpoint, a genuine env var (the ecosystem convention) won't be seen; if the host's user has an env key AND a pinned store twin, buildAgentStack's check will report drift (twin wins over empty-canonical in store-only mode) and fire the warning even though the actual request path (env, per CLI chain) would use the env var. Leg 3 skipped (not defaultEndpoint since defaultBaseUrl null). chained = null. pinnedTwin (knownSlotNames contains twin, holds value) → name = twin → driftHint fires. Now the CRITICAL correctness question I flagged: **aborted runs emit `run error`**. Let me trace once more:
1. User calls `agent.abort()` mid-request.

So yes — every user abort, every watchdog-cancel, every abort-driven run end logs `run error`. The CLI logs only `run end sid=…` for the same flow (it has no error line at all). Important detail: `formatProviderError` for `answeredHtml`/`answeredJson`/auth-redirect/empty-body cases does NOT render `<status>: ` — e.g. `'Request failed with status ${error.statusCode}'` (empty body) doesn't match `^(\d{3}): `. And `formatRateLimitMessage` renders `'<status>: <human>'` ✓. The empty-body case yields no status parse — but the typed `ProviderHttpError` branch in `_statusFromError` catches that directly (statusCode field). So `_statusFromError` handles typed errors fully; the string-parse fallback only applies to string errorMessage paths (in-stream ErrorEvents where the original error object is lost). For in-stream ErrorEvents, the errorMessage came from the provider adapters' own `formatProviderError` — consistent.

One more check on `_statusFromError`: it's called with `event.errorMessage` (a String) for in-stream ErrorEvents, and with thrown `error` objects in catch paths. In `_pump`: `if (event is ErrorEvent) _statusFromError(event.errorMessage);` — String branch. OK.

Subtle: `_statusFromError` keeps the LAST status. Multiple failed requests in one run (retry across turns): error record at run end carries the last failed status. Doc matches ("status of the failed request").

Now the CRITICAL correctness question I flagged: **aborted runs emit `run error`**. Let me trace once more:
1. User calls `agent.abort()` mid-request.
2. The loop: stream ends with aborted event OR `_abortedTurn` produces terminal message StopReason.aborted, errorMessage 'Operation aborted'.
3. AgentEndEvent messages include that terminal AssistantMessage with errorMessage != null.
4. `agentErrorMessage` returns 'Operation aborted' → `_emit(error, httpStatus: _lastHttpStatus, detail: 'Operation aborted')` → fa.log gets `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted`.

So yes — every user abort, every watchdog-cancel, every abort-driven run end logs `run error`. The CLI logs only `run end sid=…` for the same flow (it has no error line at all). For a host sharing fa.log, a forensics grep for `run error` now surfaces routine cancels. This dilutes the exact signal the issue cares about (real hangs/failures). It's a diagnostics-semantics bug worth IMPORTANT.

Wait — but is it possibly intended ("The terminal error of a finished run, or null on a clean run")? An aborted run is not a clean run. But the fa.log LINE label is `run error`, which reads as failure. And `runEnd.httpStatus` becomes null for aborted runs even if the last request 429'd. Design-wise I'd flag it: distinguish StopReason.error from StopReason.aborted in `agentErrorMessage`. IMPORTANT.

Now, another look at `AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` — it's PUBLIC. Why public? It's an instance method with no state use. Public surface bloat on the adapter; could be static or private. Minor SUGGESTION (API surface).

Also `_emit` for `error`: `httpStatus: httpStatus ?? _kindStatus(kind)` — passing `_lastHttpStatus` explicitly, `_kindStatus` returns `_lastHttpStatus` for error kind — redundant but harmless.

`runEnd`: `httpStatus: error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null` — for clean runs `_lastHttpStatus` is always null (never set on success) — so the doc "2xx when any token streamed" is dead text; runEnd NEVER carries a status in practice (error runs pass null explicitly; clean runs have null). So the httpStatus-on-runEnd feature is effectively UNIMPLEMENTED. That upgrades the doc-mismatch: the public API documents runEnd carrying "the status of the LAST request (2xx when any token streamed, else null)" but no code path can ever produce a non-null runEnd status. Either the implementation is missing the 2xx capture or the doc is wrong. IMPORTANT.

Let me also check `TurnEndEvent` for turnEnd stopReason: `message.stopReason.name` — fine.

`firstToken` semantics on turn 2+: pump emits per-request firstToken ✓ (local `first`).

`requestStart` detail: 'model=${model.id} provider=${model.provider}' — `model.provider` — does Model have `provider`? In tests Model(provider: 'test-provider') ✓.

Let me grep for `WiredAgentCore._(` to be sure. Also check `WiredAgentStack` unchanged.

Also: does `buildAgentStack` run the drift check even when `spec.model` is a wire/model whose baseUrl is a custom endpoint without activeCustomKeyName? Then chained = scoped-if-present; pinned twin via knownSlotNames. OK.

One question: the drift check resolves WITHOUT envNames — so for the DEFAULT catalog endpoint, a genuine env var (the ecosystem convention) won't be seen; if the host's user has an env key AND a pinned store twin, buildAgentStack's check will report drift (twin wins over empty-canonical in store-only mode) and fire the warning even though the actual request path (env, per CLI chain) would use the env var. Hmm wait — would it? Store-only resolution: `_firstGenuineEnvName` skipped (no defaultBaseUrl). activeCustomKeyName null → skipped. scoped FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM — empty. Leg 3 skipped (not defaultEndpoint since defaultBaseUrl null). chained = null. pinnedTwin (knownSlotNames contains twin, holds value) → name = twin → driftHint fires. But the REAL chain with catalog facts: genuine env OPENROUTER... for kimi there are no env names in the catalog? kimi's env names... For the kimi case (no env convention), store-only == full. But for e.g. openrouter with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in env AND a pinned twin in store: full chain → genuine env wins → slotName = env var, no drift. Store-only (buildAgentStack check) → twin wins → DRIFT WARNING FIRES — a FALSE POSITIVE: the run would actually bind the env key, yet the host UI shows "key slot is FA_KEY_API_..._TWIN; move the value…". The PR's contract note 3 acknowledges store-only at wiring time and tells hosts with a catalog to call resolveKey directly with envNames — but buildAgentStack's automatic check cannot know the catalog, so a catalog-host that ALSO passes knownSlotNames gets a spurious drift banner at stack build. Possible but narrow; the doc says "If you supply a keyResolver, buildAgentStack also runs this check for the run's model and fires onKeySlotDrift once" — it doesn't caveat the false-positive. Now I see the CLI's actual fa.log line format:

- `'run start sid=$_logSid'` — includes **sid=** (short session id)!
- `'turn start sid=$_logSid'`
- `'tool start sid=$_logSid name=$toolName'`
- `'tool end sid=$_logSid name=$toolName error=$isError'`
- `'turn end sid=$_logSid stop=${message.stopReason.name}'`

The new `FileAgentTelemetrySink` writes lines WITHOUT the `sid=` field: `run start`, `turn start`, `tool start name=bash`, `turn end stop=stop elapsed=7s`. The PR claims "the SAME `<iso8601> <message>` lines as the CLI" and "post-mortem-identical; grep one log for either" and "the CLI's own fa.log fidelity... line-for-line (issue #1322 AC: the same fidelity for an in-process host)". But the lines lack `sid=`, which the CLI deliberately adds ("parallel fa processes share one fa.log, so every lifecycle line names its session"). Since hosts and the CLI share ONE log file (`~/.fah/logs/fa.log`), interleaved host lines can't be attributed to a session/run while CLI lines can. The claimed "post-mortem-identical / same greps work" is materially overstated: `grep 'tool start sid='` won't match host lines, and correlating a host's interleaved lines with a specific run is impossible (no session id, no run id). The sink has no way to know the session id, and AgentCoreServices has none either. This is a real gap vs the stated AC — I'd rate this IMPORTANT (maintainability/forensics fidelity gap, misleading doc claims) — arguably it's the core deliverable promise of Gap 3. Not blocking (functionality works), but the "identical" claim is wrong. Also `elapsed=` on turn end is an ADDITION not in the CLI's format; plus `run error ... http=`. Important detail: `formatProviderError` for `answeredHtml`/`answeredJson`/auth-redirect/empty-body cases does NOT render `<status>: ` — e.g. `'Request failed with status ${error.statusCode}'` (empty body) doesn't match `^(\d{3}): `. And `formatRateLimitMessage` renders `'<status>: <human>'` ✓. The empty-body case yields no status parse — but the typed `ProviderHttpError` branch in `_statusFromError` catches that directly (statusCode field). So `_statusFromError` handles typed errors fully; the string-parse fallback only applies to string errorMessage paths (in-stream ErrorEvents where the original error object is lost). For in-stream ErrorEvents, the errorMessage came from the provider adapters' own `formatProviderError` — consistent.

One more check on `_statusFromError`: it's called with `event.errorMessage` (a String) for in-stream ErrorEvents, and with thrown `error` objects in catch paths. In `_pump`: `if (event is ErrorEvent) _statusFromError(event.errorMessage);` — String branch. OK.

Subtle: `_statusFromError` keeps the LAST status. Multiple failed requests in one run (retry across turns): error record at run end carries the last failed status. Doc matches ("status of the failed request").

Now the CRITICAL correctness question I flagged: **aborted runs emit `run error`**. Let me trace once more:
1. User calls `agent.abort()` mid-request.
2. The loop: stream ends with aborted event OR `_abortedTurn` produces terminal message StopReason.aborted, errorMessage 'Operation aborted'.
3. AgentEndEvent messages include that terminal AssistantMessage with errorMessage != null.
4. `agentErrorMessage` returns 'Operation aborted' → `_emit(error, httpStatus: _lastHttpStatus, detail: 'Operation aborted')` → fa.log gets `run error elapsed=…s: Operation aborted`.

So yes — every user abort, every watchdog-cancel, every abort-driven run end logs `run error`. The CLI logs only `run end sid=…` for the same flow (it has no error line at all). For a host sharing fa.log, a forensics grep for `run error` now surfaces routine cancels. This dilutes the exact signal the issue cares about (real hangs/failures). It's a diagnostics-semantics bug worth IMPORTANT.

Wait — but is it possibly intended ("The terminal error of a finished run, or null on a clean run")? An aborted run is not a clean run. But the fa.log LINE label is `run error`, which reads as failure. And `runEnd.httpStatus` becomes null for aborted runs even if the last request 429'd. Design-wise I'd flag it: distinguish StopReason.error from StopReason.aborted in `agentErrorMessage`. IMPORTANT.

Now, another look at `AgentTelemetry.agentErrorMessage` — it's PUBLIC. Why public? It's an instance method with no state use. Public surface bloat on the adapter; could be static or private. Minor SUGGESTION (API surface).

Also `_emit` for `error`: `httpStatus: httpStatus ?? _kindStatus(kind)` — passing `_lastHttpStatus` explicitly, `_kindStatus` returns `_lastHttpStatus` for error kind — redundant but harmless.

`runEnd`: `httpStatus: error == null ? _lastHttpStatus : null` — for clean runs `_lastHttpStatus` is always null (never set on success) — so the doc "2xx when any token streamed" is dead text; runEnd NEVER carries a status in practice (error runs pass null explicitly; clean runs have null). So the httpStatus-on-runEnd feature is effectively UNIMPLEMENTED. That upgrades the doc-mismatch: the public API documents runEnd carrying "the status of the LAST request (2xx when any token streamed, else null)" but no code path can ever produce a non-null runEnd status. Either the implementation is missing the 2xx capture or the doc is wrong. IMPORTANT.

One question: the drift check resolves WITHOUT envNames — so for the DEFAULT catalog endpoint, a genuine env var (the ecosystem convention) won't be seen; if the host's user has an env key AND a pinned store twin, buildAgentStack's check will report drift (twin wins over empty-canonical in store-only mode) and fire the warning even though the actual request path (env, per CLI chain) would use the env var. Hmm wait — would it? Store-only resolution: `_firstGenuineEnvName` skipped (no defaultBaseUrl). activeCustomKeyName null → skipped. scoped FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM — empty. Leg 3 skipped (not defaultEndpoint since defaultBaseUrl null). chained = null. pinnedTwin (knownSlotNames contains twin, holds value) → name = twin → driftHint fires. But the REAL chain with catalog facts: genuine env OPENROUTER... for kimi there are no env names in the catalog? kimi's env names... For the kimi case (no env convention), store-only == full. But for e.g. openrouter with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in env AND a pinned twin in store: full chain → genuine env wins → slotName = env var, no drift. Store-only (buildAgentStack check) → twin wins → DRIFT WARNING FIRES — a FALSE POSITIVE: the run would actually bind the env key, yet the host UI shows "key slot is FA_KEY_API_..._TWIN; move the value…". The PR's contract note 3 acknowledges store-only at wiring time and tells hosts with a catalog to call resolveKey directly with envNames — but buildAgentStack's automatic check cannot know the catalog, so a catalog-host that ALSO passes knownSlotNames gets a spurious drift banner at stack build. How likely: the host must inject knownSlotNames (opt-in) AND have env keys set. Possible but narrow; the doc says "If you supply a keyResolver, buildAgentStack also runs this check for the run's model and fires onKeySlotDrift once" — it doesn't caveat the false-positive. No dart:io ✓. The file sink has dart:io and is only exported from lib/io.dart ✓.

Let me quickly double check one potential behavioral bug in the wrap: `wrapStreamFunction` emits `requestStart` BEFORE checking anything — including for the sync-throw path — fine.

But here's one more: **`_pump` never emits `firstToken` when the first event is delivered without iteration**... no, pump iterates.

**Abort during `_pump`**: if cancelToken fires, the inner stream ends with aborted event; pump forwards; firstToken already handled. Fine.

**Multiple agents sharing one AgentTelemetry**: `buildAgentStack` creates a NEW AgentTelemetry per build (per stack) — `telemetryAdapter = AgentTelemetry(sink)` inside buildAgentStack ✓ — no cross-agent state bleed. But if a host reuses ONE AgentCoreServices to build MULTIPLE stacks concurrently with a shared FileAgentTelemetrySink — records interleave in fa.log without any correlation id (the sid= gap again). Same finding.

Now, one more possible correctness issue in `resolveEndpointKey` value step: `if (envNames.contains(name))` — name could come from the activeCustomKeyName leg which for a NON-default endpoint could theoretically also be listed in envNames (host-provided). Old code: for non-default endpoint with activeCustomKeyName holding value, returned the STORE value directly — even if envRead(activeCustomKeyName) had a different genuine value. New code: envNames.contains(activeCustomKeyName) → env wins if genuine. So IF a host lists its custom slot name in envNames (weird but possible), precedence differs from the old chain (env-over-store vs store). This is a behavior change only for names appearing in BOTH envNames and the activeCustomKeyName leg. The CLI's usage: envNames = catalog names (OPENROUTER_API_KEY...), activeCustomKeyName = FA_KEY_... — disjoint in practice. Negligible; not worth flagging? It IS a subtle semantic broadening: "value and slot can never disagree" is achieved by re-consulting env for ANY name in envNames. I'll skip or fold into the parity note as a nit. Skip.

Now — check `docs/embedding.md` claim: "The CLI (bin/fah.dart) is itself just the first host shell built on exactly this layer (lib/src/hosts/host_agent_wiring.dart)". True post-#1230.

content.thinking:
A few more observations from this read:

1. `agentErrorMessage` doc: "The agent loop stores the last failed assistant turn's message on the agent state; [event]'s messages carry the same field." — first sentence is confusing/stale-ish but harmless.

2. **Aborted runs → `run error` record** (confirmed above). Also note: `StopReason.aborted` messages carry errorMessage 'Operation aborted' → error record. IMPORTANT finding.

3. **`error` record on AgentEndEvent uses `_lastHttpStatus`** — for a run whose LAST request failed mid-turn N but a LATER turn's request succeeded... wait, if a later request succeeded, the run ends clean (no error message) → no error record. If the run ends with error, the last request is the failed one. Actually not exactly: turn 1 request fails (429) → terminal error turn → run ends. Fine. But context-window-exhausted error ("the outgoing context is ~N tokens... The request was not sent") — that's an error turn WITHOUT a request; if an earlier request in the same run 429'd... no — a 429 terminal ends the run. Mixed sequences are unlikely. OK.

4. **`_errorEventFor` drops `cancelToken` abort semantics**: if the wrapped inner throws due to ABORT (some adapters may throw on abort? contract says never throw — they return aborted events), the wrap would convert an abort-throw into StopReason.error instead of aborted. Only for out-of-contract stream functions. Minor, skip.

5. `_pump` catch pushes `_errorEventFor` but does NOT `outer.end()` in the catch — it does in `finally` ✓.

6. In the sync-throw path: `outer.push(...); outer.end();` ✓.

7. `unawaited(_pump(...))` — if the HOST never subscribes to outer, and the inner stream never terminates (hang), the pump awaits forever — a leaked pending future per hung request. Same as legacy (the loop would also hang). Fine.

8. **Record ordering race — `requestStart` emitted synchronously at call time; the agent's `AgentStartEvent` fires BEFORE the loop calls streamFunction** ✓ ordering: runStart, turnStart, requestStart ✓ (test asserts exactly this order).

9. `MessageUpdateEvent() when !_sawFirstToken` — after the run's first pump-firstToken, `_sawFirstToken` stays true for the whole run; the fallback never fires again — by design.

Edge: **a run where the stream function is wrapped BUT the first provider event arrives while `_sawFirstToken` false and pump sets it — no double** ✓.

10. `sinceRunStart` uses two separate `DateTime.now()` calls (timestamp + difference) — microsecond-level skew; negligible nit. Skip.

Now the file sink — `record` writes `DateTime.now().toIso8601String()` rather than `event.timestamp`: the CLI also uses now() at write time ✓ parity.

`firstToken` line: `'first token ${event.detail ?? ''}'` — detail is set by the pump's `_emit(firstToken)` WITHOUT detail! In `_pump`: `_emit(AgentTelemetryEventKind.firstToken);` — no detail. But in the fallback path in `_record` (MessageUpdateEvent), also `_emit(firstToken)` no detail. So the actual firstToken line is `first token ` with a TRAILING SPACE (detail null → `'first token ' + ''`). Look at the file sink: `'first token ${event.detail ?? ''}'` → "first token " — trailing whitespace line. The TEST works around this by passing detail explicitly (`_event(firstToken, detail: 'model=...')`) — the test does NOT exercise the adapter's real firstToken record through the sink! In the real wiring, every `first token` fa.log line will have a trailing space. Cosmetic, but it also means model/provider context is missing from the real firstToken lines (the requestStart line right before has it, so attribution is fine). Minor SUGGESTION: either pass detail on firstToken in the pump (matching the sink's expectation and the test) or trim in the sink. This is a real (if small) defect: the sink API clearly expects firstToken detail ('model=... provider=...') — the pump never supplies it. I'll flag as SUGGESTION.

Also `requestStart` line: `'request start ${event.detail}'` — detail null → "request start null"! When could requestStart lack detail? The wrap always passes detail. But the Sink API accepting a null-detail requestStart renders "request start null" — same class of nit as above. The `_event()` helper in tests defaults detail to null but tests pass detail for requestStart. Defensive formatting nit — fold into the same suggestion.

Also `toolHeartbeat`/`toolStuck` lines: `'tool heartbeat name=$name ${event.detail}'` — detail always set by adapter ✓; null → "null" again. Same nit family.

11. `InMemoryTelemetrySink.events` — `List.unmodifiable` ✓.

12. Wire-up: `AgentCoreServices.telemetry` doc says "Null = silent (today's behavior)" ✓.

13. Test gap: no test covers `FileAgentTelemetrySink` receiving an adapter-produced firstToken (trailing-space case) — noted above. Also no test for the aborted-run error record (because it's unflagged behavior). And no test for `_statusFromError` via typed ProviderHttpError through `_pump` catch (covered via sync-throw test).

14. **`docs/embedding.md` example bug**: `if (resolution?.slotName == null) { myUi.showBanner(resolution!.missingKeyHint!); }` — when keyResolver is null, `services.resolveKey` returns null → `resolution?.slotName == null` is true → `resolution!` throws (null check). In the doc's context a resolver IS set, but the snippet is presented as a general pattern. A safer pattern: `final resolution = services.resolveKey(...); if (resolution != null && resolution.slotName == null) ...`. SUGGESTION (docs).

15. `HostKeyResolver` doc for `knownSlotNames` says "A known pinned twin of the canonical (`<canonical>_…`) holding a value wins over the canonical" — implementation: wins over canonical-or-nothing ✓.

16. `resolveKey` — `provider` unused except hint text; `model` unused (documented). Lint-wise fine (named params).

17. Thread-safety: single isolate — fine.

18. **Exports/docs**: `AgentTelemetry`/`InMemoryTelemetrySink`/etc. now public API via the barrel — no `@doc` on the barrel itself; fine.

19. The `default:` case in `_record` swallows `AgentSettledEvent` silently — the comment lists "MessageStart/End, ModelRequest, pairing repair, partial updates" — could mention AgentSettledEvent; skip.

20. File sink `_dirEnsured` — set true before createSync; if the FIRST create fails (transient), later records never retry dir creation. Deliberate simplicity; silent anyway. Skip (or mention in passing).

21. `CHANGELOG` — convention followed. Skip.

22. `pr_info` claims "Phase map mirrors the CLI's fa.log forensics (…heartbeat/stuck)" — CLI heartbeat line includes `out=…B attempt=…` which the adapter drops (AgentTelemetryEvent lacks outputBytes/attempt fields). The sink's heartbeat line therefore has less forensic content than the CLI's. Part of the "fidelity" finding with sid=. Combine into the IMPORTANT finding about fa.log fidelity claims (sid missing; heartbeat out/attempt dropped).

23. Check `test/hosts/host_agent_wiring_test.dart` — `_textTurnCalls` global mutable — if the test suite is shuffled/retried, counter only asserted `== 1` after exactly one prompt in that test; other tests don't touch `_textTurnStream`. Fine.

24. `fullServices` helper change — telemetry/keyResolver/onKeySlotDrift default null — existing callers unaffected ✓.

25. One more: **`buildAgentStack` drift-check placement** — fires `onKeySlotDrift` even when the model resolves fine (only when hint != null) ✓.

26. `HostKeyResolution.fromEnv` — for chained legacy-store names in envNames (leg 3), `_isGenuineEnv` false → fromEnv false ✓ correct (it's from store).

27. Docs: "`final streamFn = providerStreamFunction('openai-completions', apiKey,)`" — kind list comment "openai-completions, zai, anthropic, google, …" ✓ matches catalog kinds.

28. Docs: "`wireAgentCore(profile: cliProfile, services: services)`" — `cliProfile` exported? Let me check the barrel for host_capability_profile exports (cliProfile).
